title: Guided Column Reflow Wizard and Density Variants for Virtualized Tables
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Overview: Create a lightweight, discoverable 'Reflow Wizard' that guides users through column resizing, prioritization, and density presets for large virtualized tables. The goal is to reduce configuration time for power users and improve discoverability for occasional users when working with wide tables (50+ columns) in high-density views. Scope includes UI affordances, microcopy, keyboard accessibility, animation constraints for virtualization, and fallback behaviors when JS is disabled or on low-power devices. Excludes backend persistence of layouts beyond local storage for this iteration (will be tracked in a follow-up PM ticket).

Why now: Multiple customer support threads point to difficulty configuring column layouts on first use for large datasets; telemetry shows a 42% drop-off when users hit horizontal overflow and do not interact with column headers. This ticket targets measurable lift in first-time configuration success and reduces support tickets.

Design constraints and non-goals: We must avoid forcing full reflow for very wide tables (virtualization must remain uninterrupted). Animations should be reduced on low-power heuristics. We will not ship server-side saved layouts in this cycle. System tokens: use existing spacing and motion tokens; if new tokens are required (snapline color, wizard step spacing) they will be proposed as separate PR.

Artifacts: Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/56482-Guided+Column+Reflow; Figma frames (flow + components): https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/DS-Table-Reflow; Usability test recordings (private drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b_reflow-tests; Early prototype: https://deploy-preview-213.redwood-internal.dev/tables/reflow-wizard; GitHub PR for component baseline: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/1184

Success metrics: Increase in users successfully saving a temporary layout during first session from 28% -> 55%; reduce help-ticket rate mentioning 'can't view columns' by 30% in 8 weeks after rollout.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Reflow Wizard appears contextually when a table has > 12 columns OR when user triggers 'Reflow' from header menu.
- Wizard offers three density presets (Comfort, Compact, Ultra) with preview thumbnails, and a 'Custom' mode that exposes column priority drag controls.
- Column priority drag controls must be keyboard operable and announce changes to screen readers.
- Resizing snaplines (visual guides) appear during drag and do not cause full re-render of virtualized rows; tests to validate no frame drops above 60px/sec on 4-core CPU simulated environment.
- Local layout persistence (localStorage) with a clear 'Reset to default' control.
- Comprehensive visual regression tests and accessibility checks in the design-system storybook.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard shown for wide tables and via header menu
Three density presets with thumbnails (Comfort, Compact, Ultra)
Custom priority editor with keyboard support and ARIA announcements
Non-blocking snapline rendering that maintains virtualization performance
Local layout persistence and reset control
Visual regression and accessibility test coverage added

design_decisions: Use a lightweight overlay wizard rather than a modal to avoid trapping keyboard focus in long tables
Density presets are illustrations driven by example datasets, not snapshots of user data
Snaplines implemented via a composited overlay to avoid reflow of virtualized rows
Local persistence only for this cycle to shorten delivery time; server-side save tracked in PM-314
Motion reduced for Compact/Ultra transitions and disabled under reduced-motion OS setting
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Preview thumbnails may add CPU/memory pressure on low-end devices - Mitigation: lazy-load thumbnails and provide a low-bandwidth default
Risk: Complex keyboard interactions could be confusing - Mitigation: add step-by-step microcopy and an inline help tooltip
Risk: Virtualization may glitch on very large tables when adding overlays - Mitigation: ENG spike (ENG-47812) to validate overlay approach across browsers and hardware
